proposals.evidence: The full DEDR 410 article gives Malayalam i, ī this; ivaṇ, ivaḷ, ivar, itu, iva this man, this woman, these persons, this thing, these things; iṅṅu in this direction, here; iṅṅanē, iṅṅinē thus; iṅṅiṭē, iṅṅiṭa here, hither; iṅṅōṭṭu hither, this way; itā behold here!; ittaram this kind, thus;…. The Byari survey form ivlu “third-person singular, female, proximate” is proposed within this article family. Lindgren assigns the corresponding Tamil reflex to the same source cognate set.

proposals.evidence: The full DEDR 1 article gives Malayalam a, ā that, yonder; avan, avaḷ, avar, atu, ava that man, that woman, those persons, that thing, those things; atatu each, several; aṅṅu, aṅṅunnu there, thither; aṅṅane, aṅṅine that way, thus; aṅṅiṭam, aṅṅōṭu there; aṅṅiṭ-iṅṅiṭam here and there; atā…. The Byari survey form avlu “third-person singular, female, remote” is proposed within this article family. Lindgren assigns the corresponding Tamil reflex to the same source cognate set.
